skills.name: assert-fact-gate
skills.description: Use BEFORE asserting any SHA, file content, route, build, status, test result, or identifier. Forces a fresh source-check this turn so claims are verified, not recalled. Triggers on "the build is", "the file says", "X passed/green", "the SHA is", "it's deployed", or any factual claim about repo / infra / test / handoff state.

skills.name: ci-security-scanning-with-strix
skills.description: Add security scanning to CI/CD with Strix — GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or any pipeline — so every pull request gets a diff-scoped AI pentest that blocks vulnerable code before it merges, with results as PR comments and SARIF uploaded to code scanning. Covers both the self-hosted open-source CLI (runs in your runner) and the managed app.strix.ai platform (GitHub/GitLab app or API, no runner infra). Use when the user asks to add security scanning, SAST/DAST, pentesting, vulnerability checks, or automated security review to their CI pipeline, pre-merge gate, or PR workflow.

skills.name: deploy-gate

skills.name: fix-security-vulnerabilities-with-strix
skills.description: Fix security vulnerabilities found by a Strix pentest (open-source CLI or app.strix.ai cloud) — triage by severity, patch the root cause rather than the symptom, and re-run Strix to prove each fix actually closes the exploit. Handles injection, XSS, SSRF, broken access control, IDOR, and other validated findings. Use after a Strix scan reports findings, or when the user asks to remediate, patch, or fix security issues from a strix_runs report, vulnerabilities.json, findings.sarif, or a cloud scan.

skills.name: gavel
skills.description: Gavel - typed judgments for a project lead's decisions. Before you rule on a worker's return, send a handoff, or order a backlog, ask a fixed set of narrow questions and get typed answers with probabilities: disposition (accept / rework / withdraw / consult owner / answer questions), evidence quality, silent gaps, scope creep, irreversibility, next owner, urgency; whether a draft handoff carries a receipt contract; how gate-blocking and risky each backlog item is. Powered by TypeSafe's System One model (Jev) through a bundled stdlib helper. Use when triaging a return, handback or consult; before sending any handoff; when prioritising a checklist; whenever a lead decision should be checked against calibrated common sense. Works in any project, any harness, any model.

skills.name: infra-naming-gate
skills.description: Use BEFORE creating, renaming, provisioning, documenting, or approving Kaidera infrastructure resources such as VMs, runtime hosts, databases, load balancers, clusters, namespaces, service accounts, buckets, Helm releases, Argo apps, network policies, or project-runtime planes. Validates names against the canonical infrastructure naming SOP and cloud-agnostic policy.

skills.name: kaidera-sdlc
skills.description: The Kaidera AI-native SDLC: the operating loop every lead runs for an epic, feature, fix, incident, review or plan. Capture intent, grill it one question at a time, spec with policy applied, plan before any code, build inside a feedback loop, verify with output that can fail, review adversarially, ship through deterministic gates, close the loop from production. Use when starting or scoping any work, when a handoff or incident arrives, when asked to plan, spec, grill, interview, stress-test, review, retro or ship, and when deciding what done means.

skills.name: managed-pentesting-with-strix
skills.description: Run a managed pentest of a web app or API through the app.strix.ai REST API — no local Docker, LLM key, or install needed. Create an API token, register domain/repository assets, launch and poll scans, triage vulnerabilities, export SARIF, download PDF/DOCX pentest reports for SOC 2 and other compliance evidence (Enterprise plan), start PR reviews, and set up schedules and webhooks. Use when the user wants continuous or scheduled pentesting-as-a-service, an auditor-ready pentest report, scans tracked in a team dashboard, or security testing from a sandboxed agent/CI environment with no infrastructure.

skills.name: open-code-review

Use this for a bounded change review; use a whole-codebase audit skill for repository-wide health or architecture assessment.

rules.title: Canonical architecture (CTO ruling R5, 2026-09-02)
rules.body:
# Canonical architecture — consult before any deployment, runtime or packaging work

Kaidera OS ships as a **Linux VM appliance** (CTO ruling R5, 2026-09-02, design 26):

1. The **KOS console runs natively** on the VM as a service (the app, the SPA, the
   orchestrator, the terminal PTY lane).
2. **Harness CLIs are installed locally** on the VM: OpenKai is the primary, first-party
   harness (installed at a pinned release); omp is installed and supported until OpenKai is
   mature; claude-code and codex are optional, customer-installed, and supported when present
   locally. Every lane is a PTY-attached child process of the console.
3. **Cortex and its services are seven podman containers** (db, migrate, cortex-api,
   project-bootstrap, graph/embed/pdf workers) managed by `kos` from the control-volume
   contract, named volumes and the lifecycle journal, published on loopback only.
4. **Host family:** Fedora/RHEL (Rocky/Alma 10 for hosts we control, RHEL for customers);
   Ubuntu supported behind the podman ≥ 5 preflight. **Commercial ships Linux only.**
5. **macOS is a development environment only:** the same shape with the services in podman
   machine (never Apple Container). Windows is not a target.

Reliability, control and the security layers are specified in the ontology
(`docs/design/KOS_ONTOLOGY.md` §11b). The current-state contract is
`docs/CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE_AND_RELEASE.md`; the decision record is
`docs/design/26-portable-appliance-assessment.md`. Live Cortex beats docs; if this rule and a
document disagree, raise it as a handoff instead of guessing.

rules.title: Cloud policy: AWS only, no Google Cloud
rules.body: Cloud policy (CTO decision 2026-09-17, docs/design/40-aws-only-no-google.md): Kaidera OS infrastructure is AWS only (account 417007889577, us-east-1). Do not create, propose, or depend on any Google Cloud resource or Google service (GCE, GCS, Cloud Build, Google IAM, Google DNS, Google CI). Backups and migration artifacts go to S3 bucket kos-backup-417007889577-us-east-1 (Glacier Instant Retrieval for restorable artifacts, Standard only for hot working copies). Secrets go to AWS Secrets Manager or Vaultwarden, never a laptop file or chat. Hosts are EC2 or the ASW k3s cluster with scheduled EBS snapshots and a rehearsed restore drill. Existing Google Cloud resources are exit-only: capture, verify on AWS, then delete on a CTO line. Exception: Google Workspace data that products still read (Wren wrendrive Google Drive FileVault) stays until the CTO rules on its own migration; do not add new Workspace dependencies. If a task needs something only Google offers, raise a consult handoff to kai instead of building it. ACCESS METHOD (CTO SOP 2026-09-18, design 40 rules 6-8): agents reach AWS through the API with the access key pair in the project .env, read by name (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY); never aws login, IAM Identity Center / SSO, a browser or console sign-in, or a named profile. Every script that calls AWS sets AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null and AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null, loads the two keys with a command substitution (not source <(...)), and fails closed first: both variables non-empty and aws sts get-caller-identity succeeds. Key values are never printed, logged, committed or sent anywhere except to AWS.

rules.title: code-graph-tool
rules.body:
# Code Review Graph Tool

Local structural code graphs are available through the Cortex graph commands and
the `better-code-review-graph` database when present.

Use them for token-efficient structural questions: blast radius, callers,
callees, imports, risk hotspots, and test coverage.

## Boundary Rule

Always point graph tooling at the repository or workspace you are actively
editing. For this project, the normal root is:

```text
/Users/amadmalik/DevVault/helix
```

Do not infer Kaidera AI platform topology from helix graph results, and do not
use Kaidera AI repo roots while working in helix unless the CTO explicitly asks
for a cross-project filesystem review.

## Preferred Cortex Commands

```bash
cortex-graph-blast --target .agents/api/main.py --repo helix --max-results 20
cortex-graph-callers <function-or-symbol>
cortex-graph-impact <file-or-change>
cortex-graph-large-fn
cortex-graph-stats
```

Use graph output as implementation guidance, not as a substitute for tests.

## Direct Library Fallback

If a direct `better-code-review-graph` query is needed:

```bash
uv tool run --from better-code-review-graph python -c "
from better_code_review_graph import tools
import json
result = tools.query_graph(
    pattern='file_summary',
    target='.agents/api/main.py',
    repo_root='/Users/amadmalik/DevVault/helix'
)
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))
"
```

Replace `target` with the actual symbol or file under review.

rules.title: cortex
rules.body:
# Cortex — Agent Session Rules

**Version:** v2.5 Phase A rules (Kaidera OS-owned)
**Audience:** the local Cortex dev-team agents running on this Mac — current roster naming **Alpha / Root / Lux / Hue / Sam / Scribe**, plus the Kaidera OS co-leads **Kai** and **Ren** under the internal `helix` project key. (The old names *Keith / Sophi / Marv / Hue* were Kaidera AI *commercial-platform* personas, NOT the dev team — do not use them.) These rules apply to every agent operating in the local Cortex on this Mac, across the projects we run locally.
**Local Cortex API:** `http://localhost:8501` — the loopback dogfood service on this Mac. The Kaidera AI *commercial platform* Cortex is a separately deployed service; do not confuse it with this local service. (See the Separation Model below.)
**Kaidera OS-owned file.** This is Kaidera OS's own rules file at `helix/cortex.md`; `.agents/rules/cortex.md` and `.claude/rules/cortex.md` symlink to it. **There is no shared parent file** — Kaidera OS is a complete split from the other projects and owns its own rules; edit this copy freely for Kaidera OS.

---

## Separation Model

Treat these as three different layers. Do not collapse them.

- **Local Cortex** is the loopback service on this Mac at `http://localhost:8501` with local PostgreSQL. It is for personal use, dogfooding, imports, and agent workflow support on this machine only.
- **Kaidera AI Platform Cortex** is the commercial platform architecture, deployment model, tenancy model, and production memory boundary for Kaidera AI. It is not defined by the local stack. It is out of scope for the helix team (Kai/Ren).
- **External Project Cortex** covers separate projects or customers such as Kaidera AI, ASW Connect, ASW Events, TAM-DEV, or Paul. Those remain independent scopes even if their artifacts are reviewed or imported locally for learning.

Required discipline:

- Never infer Kaidera AI platform infrastructure from Local Cortex defaults.
- Never infer one external project's infrastructure, roles, or deployment from another project's Cortex files.
- Imported external artifacts are reference material only until the current project explicitly adopts the learning.
- If an external project artifact is copied into a workspace, keep it clearly labeled as external and non-authoritative.
- In a program workspace such as Kaidera AI, separate component repos may share Cortex coordination while remaining independent services and independent deployment units.
- A shared workspace registry is not a monorepo release contract. Pushes, branches, and deployments still happen at the actual repo boundary.
- Shared Cortex coordination is not blanket permission for cross-project edits. The May 2026 Cortex-before-CAG/RAG sweep was a one-off CTO-approved exception; future cross-project edits, posts, migrations, or documentation sweeps require explicit CTO consent before work starts.

Authority order:

- current project's runtime config, live `cortex-boot`, and current workspace docs
- canonical shared rules in this file
- explicitly imported external learnings

## Cortex 6-Layer Architecture

Full local-Cortex design lives at `local-cortex/ARCHITECTURE.md` with the visual at `local-cortex/architecture.excalidraw.md`. This is dev-team local Cortex, not the customer-platform Cortex.

| Layer | Status | What |
|---|---|---|
| L6 Boot Context | KEEP | `cortex-boot` pulls identity, facts, and recent history for session start |
| L5 Multimodal Artifacts | NEW | `artifacts` + `artifact_edges` with typed modality, captions, neighborhood text, and provenance |
| L4 Knowledge Graph | NEW | `cortex_entities` + `cortex_relationships` with LightRAG-style dual-level retrieval |
| L3 Code Graph | OPTIMIZE | `better-code-review-graph` via DuckDB + SQLite, exposed through `cortex-graph-*` |
| L2 Vector Embeddings | KEEP | pgvector 768-d embeddings over durable text rows |
| L1 Verbatim Storage | KEEP | decisions, lessons, knowledge, messages, handoffs, tasks, agents, and artifacts |

Retrieval surfaces:

- `cortex-search "<exact phrase or id>"` for exact handoff IDs, exact CTO phrases, exact document titles, and exact incident strings.
- `cortex-graph-search "<query>" --limit 5` for broad architecture, epic, service, tool, process, and thematic recall.
- `cortex-graph-search "<query>" --expand --limit 5` only when the top graph hit is useful and one-hop relationship context is needed.
- `cortex-entities --search "<entity>"` or `cortex-entities --related "<entity>"` for direct Layer 4 entity browsing.
- `cortex-graph-blast --target <function-or-file> --repo <repo>` before touching shared code.

Retrieval routing note: graph search is faster and smaller in aggregate, but it is NOT a full replacement for exact-string search. A/B validation showed large aggregate token + latency wins and improved precision overall, yet exact-string recall (handoff IDs, exact phrases, incident strings) still needs the `cortex-search` fallback. Don't over-claim a blanket "60% better".

## Phase A Operating Rules

### Search routing

- `cortex-graph-search "<query>" --limit 5` for thematic, architecture, epic, service, tool, and process questions.
- `cortex-search "<exact phrase>"` for exact handoff IDs, exact CTO phrases, exact document titles, and exact incident strings.
- `cortex-graph-search "<query>" --expand --limit 5` only when the top entity hit is useful and one-hop context is needed.
- Do not repeat "60% better" as a blanket claim. A/B validation partially validated the aggregate performance direction; exact-string recall still needs the `cortex-search` fallback.

### Blast-radius mandate

- Run `cortex-graph-blast <file> --repo .` before editing shared code.
- This is a hard rule for cross-cutting code paths and a required handoff receipt when delegating risky work.

### Logging cadence

- Fifteen minutes without a meaningful Cortex log is under-logging.
- Log a decision when starting or finishing a task.
- Log a lesson when the rule should survive beyond the current task.
- Use `cortex-save-chat <agent> <topic> "..."` at session end when the session produced meaningful context.

## Session Start

```bash
export PATH=$PATH:$(pwd)/.agents/scripts
cortex-boot <your-name>
```

`cortex-boot` is the source of truth for your current identity and project.
It gives you:
- your identity as `<name>@<project>` (e.g. `ren@helix`)
- pending handoffs with their bare UUIDs
- recent decisions, lessons, and infrastructure context

For topic focus:

```bash
cortex-boot <your-name> --query "steering"
```

---

## Identity Discipline

**Identity v2 (2026-06-15) retired the old colon-suffixed compound identity.** Identity is now *derived* by the Cortex
API, never a stored hex. You never construct, guess, or store a 4-char project hex.

- Your working identity is `<agent_name>@<project_key>` (e.g. `ren@helix`, `kai@helix`). Use this exact
  form in every human-readable Cortex write (log summaries, handoff summaries, progress, blocked notices).
- Handoff references use the **bare UUID** (e.g. `5e7b7a7e-8f07-40b2-a4b3-d7c91b040248`) — no suffix.
- The **retired** colon-suffixed / hex-derived forms are now **rejected by the write path
  (HTTP 400)**. Never put a colon suffix or project-derived short code in new memory rows, summaries, or handoffs.
- If docs and live Cortex disagree, trust live Cortex.

Source of truth for your identity + project:
- the identity line from `cortex-boot <name>` ("You are `<name>@<project>`, an agent on the `<project>` project")
- handoff IDs shown by `cortex-handoff` (bare UUIDs)
- the project entry from `cortex-projects`

If you are unsure of your identity, re-run `cortex-boot <name>`.

---

## Never touch the Cortex database directly

The Cortex Postgres container (`cortex-pg`) is a datastore, not an
interface. Do not:

- `docker exec cortex-pg psql ...` to read or write data
- Run `psql -h localhost -p 5499 ...` against the Cortex DB
- `docker exec` into Cortex containers for any operational step
- Install, migrate, or configure Kaidera AI platform components onto the
  local Cortex Postgres (it is not your project DB)

Always use the HTTP API or CLI instead:

- List handoffs — `cortex-handoff --mine <agent>` or `GET /handoffs`
- Read one handoff in full — `cortex-handoff --show <id>` or
  `GET /handoffs/{id}`
- Write — `cortex-handoff --create ...` or `POST /handoffs`
- Claim / complete — `cortex-handoff --claim <id>` / `--complete <id>`
- Log decisions / lessons — `cortex-log <agent> decision "..."` or
  `POST /log`
- Search — `cortex-search "..."` or `GET /search`
- Admin surface — `/admin/*` endpoints for anything beyond

If the CLI or API does not expose what you need, that is a **tooling
gap, not a permission to reach for `psql`**. File a handoff for the
missing endpoint. Working around the API means the next agent will
copy the workaround, and the reason we have one surface is so CTO can
trust it will not be mutated out from under them.

---

## Never run project application stacks locally

Local Docker on this Mac is reserved for **the local Cortex stack only**
— the `cortex-*` containers under the `kaidera-os-cortex` compose project.
Nothing else (no customer/project application stacks).

Per-project application stacks (e.g. `asw-connect/services/docker-
compose.yml` with `asw-db` + `asw-redis`, or any `services/` compose
file in a customer project) are **deployed to GCP via CI/CD**. They
have their own compose files in-repo as reference material but those
compose files carry an explicit WARNING at the top saying do not run
locally.

Do not:

- `docker compose up` from any `services/docker-compose.yml` in a
  customer or external project repo
- Start a container named `asw-*`, `paul-*`, `tam-*`, or any other
  project-scoped service on this Mac
- Create ad-hoc test DB containers (e.g. `cortex-svc-test`) and leave
  them running — tear them down when your test session ends

If you think you need a local app stack to debug, **ask first**. The
user's local Mac is a coordination workspace, not a customer-app
runtime. Standard postgres/redis ports (5432 / 6379) must stay free
for future local-development needs.

The local Cortex stack (`kaidera-os-cortex` compose project) is a multi-container
deployment — NOT "only three". Expected running containers:

- `cortex-pg` — Cortex agent memory DB (Postgres + pgvector; port 5499, not 5432; named volume `cortex-pg-data`)
- `cortex-api` — Cortex HTTP API (port 8501)
- worker tier: `cortex-graph-worker`, `cortex-embed-worker`, `cortex-pdf-worker` (plus `cortex-audio-worker` / `cortex-vision-worker` under the `full` compose profile)

**Redis is retired from the Kaidera OS stack.** The internal `helix` compose defines no redis
service, the API holds no redis connection (`event_backend=postgres`), and the
`rcli`/`prcli` helpers were removed in the API-only migration (Postgres is the
single source of truth). Do not reintroduce a redis container or any
redis-dependent code path in Kaidera OS.

If a leftover `cortex-redis` container appears, treat it as a retired artifact:
do not route new code through it, do not depend on it for writes, and verify the
owning compose file before deleting data volumes.

Degraded modes: if `cortex-embed-worker` is down, new rows persist with NULL
embeddings and the `cortex-embed` cron backfills; graph/pdf worker outages
degrade L4/L5 enrichment only, never core L1/L2 writes. (See
`local-cortex/ARCHITECTURE.md`.) The legacy "only three containers" rule is
obsolete.

---

## Session End

```bash
cortex-diary <your-name> --write \
  --summary "what you did and decided" \
  --outcome completed \
  --importance 8
```

Outcomes: `completed` / `blocked` / `handed-off` / `partial`
Importance: 1–10. At `8` or above, it surfaces in future boots.

---

## Your Identity

Your working identity is always:

```text
<agent_name>@<project_key>
```

(e.g. `ren@helix`, `kai@helix`.) The Cortex API derives this display — you never build or store a hex.
The retired colon-suffixed compound form is **rejected by the write path**.

Use this identity anywhere another agent, a co-lead, or the orchestrator (Beat/Alpha) will read your text:
- log summaries
- handoff summaries
- progress updates
- blocked notices
- session-ending notes

CLI arguments take the plain agent name; the summary text inside those commands uses the `<name>@<project>` form.

Examples:
- `cortex-log ren decision "ren@helix fixed boot caching"`
- `cortex-handoff --claim 84b407c8-... --agent ren`
- `cortex-handoff --create --from ren --from-role full-stack-developer --to kai --summary "ren@helix BLOCKED on 84b407c8-...: waiting on migration review"`

---

## Handoff Flow

**Claim work:**
```bash
cortex-handoff --mine <name>
cortex-handoff --claim <uuid> --agent <name>
```

**Close on completion:**
```bash
cortex-handoff --complete <uuid>
```

**If blocked:**
```bash
cortex-handoff --create --from <name> --from-role <role> --to cpo \
  --summary "<name>@<project> BLOCKED on <uuid>: <reason>" \
  --priority urgent
```

**If session ends with work incomplete:**
```bash
cortex-handoff --create --from <name> --from-role <role> --to cpo \
  --summary "<name>@<project> SESSION ENDING — <uuid>: done <X>, remaining <Y>" \
  --priority high
cortex-handoff --complete <uuid>
```

Every claimed handoff closes before the session ends.

---

## Progress Cadence

**More than 15 minutes on a task:**
```bash
cortex-log <name> decision "<name>@<project> PROGRESS on <uuid>: done X, remaining Y"
```

**More than 30 minutes:**
```bash
cortex-handoff --create --from <name> --from-role <role> --to cpo \
  --summary "<name>@<project> IN PROGRESS — <uuid>: 60% done, ETA 20min" \
  --priority low
```

---

## Communication

All coordination goes through the project CPO or orchestrator handoff flow. No direct agent-to-agent side channel.

```text
You → handoff to project coordinator → coordinator → handoff to other agent
```

Keep your `<name>@<project>` identity and the bare handoff UUID in every coordination message.

---

## Daily Commands

```text
cortex-boot <name>                                                  session start
cortex-log <name> decision "<name>@<project> starting <work>"   log start
cortex-log <name> decision "..."                                    log decisions
cortex-log <name> lesson "..."                                      log lessons
cortex-search "<topic>" --room "<epic>"                             recall context
cortex-verify --file-exists <path>                                  verify a claim
cortex-handoff --complete <uuid>                        close handoff
cortex-diary <name> --write ...                                     session end
```

---

## Command Reference

### Session
| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cortex-boot <name>` | Session start — identity + context |
| `cortex-boot <name> --query <topic>` | Session start + topic recall |
| `cortex-diary <name> --write --summary "text" --outcome completed --importance N` | Session end diary |
| `cortex-onboard <name>` | First-session onboarding |

### Memory
| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cortex-log <name> decision "text"` | Log a decision |
| `cortex-log <name> lesson "text"` | Log a lesson |
| `cortex-search "query"` | Search Cortex |
| `cortex-search "query" --room "E61"` | Scoped search |
| `cortex-invalidate <id>` | Mark a decision, lesson, or handoff superseded |

### Coordination
| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cortex-handoff --mine <name>` | Your handoffs, shown as bare `uuid` |
| `cortex-handoff --claim <uuid> --agent <name>` | Claim handoff |
| `cortex-handoff --complete <uuid>` | Complete handoff |
| `cortex-handoff --create --from <name> --from-role <role> --to <role> --summary "text"` | Create handoff |
| `cortex-board --mine <name>` | Your tasks |
| `cortex-state` | Project overview |
| `cortex-roster` | Team roster |
| `cortex-projects` | Registered projects with their keys |

### Verification
| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `cortex-verify --file-exists <path>` | File exists? |
| `cortex-verify --function-exists <fn> --repo .` | Function in code? |
| `cortex-verify --decision "text"` | Active decision matches? |
| `cortex-verify --callers <fn> --min 3 --repo .` | Caller count? |

---

## Direct API

Use the CLI by default. If you must call the API directly:

```bash
# Boot
curl "http://localhost:8501/boot/<agent_name>" \
  -H "X-Project: <project_key>"

# Log
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8501/log" \
  -H "X-Agent-Name: <agent_name>" \
  -H "X-Project: <project_key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"event_type":"decision","summary":"<agent_name>@<project> decided ..."}'

# Search
curl "http://localhost:8501/search?q=<query>" \
  -H "X-Project: <project_key>"

# Create handoff
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8501/handoffs" \
  -H "X-Agent-Name: <agent_name>" \
  -H "X-Project: <project_key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to_role":"cpo","priority":"high","summary":"<agent_name>@<project> handoff for <uuid>"}'
```

For direct API calls, `X-Agent-Name` remains the plain canonical agent name, but any human-readable summary text should use the `<name>@<project>` form.

---

## Cortex v2.3 Features

All default agent operations go through the Cortex API. Do not bypass the API for normal work.

- `cortex-boot` uses priority tiers and preserves identity plus handoffs first
- `cortex-search` uses API-first retrieval and tracks result quality
- `cortex-board`, `cortex-handoff`, `cortex-state`, `cortex-roster`, `cortex-history`, and `cortex-projects` are API-backed
- execution analysis, captured patterns, degradation monitoring, and decision lineage are server-side features

Cortex derives your `<name>@<project>` identity; the retired colon-suffixed forms are rejected in new rows.

rules.title: Tools and skills are harness-agnostic: no vendor plugins or harness-only installs
rules.body: CTO permanent rule 2026-09-17 (docs/design/41-harness-agnostic-tools-only.md, THE_WAY s17): every skill, tool and integration the team adopts must work with any harness and any model. Skills are plain files under .agents/skills/<slug>/; third-party skills are installed with the agnostic CLI (npx skills add <owner>/<repo> --skill <name> -a universal -y --copy), reviewed before use, and pinned in skills-lock.json; distribution is Cortex (cortex-skill install / bind, cortex-boot, the generated neutral pointer AGENTS.md - CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are symlinks to it and are never hand-edited). Do not install, depend on, or reference a vendor plugin, marketplace, IDE add-on or harness-only extension (no claude plugin, no Codex-only or Gemini-only tool, no vendor-tied MCP server). Helpers are stdlib-first, call HTTP APIs or CLIs any agent can run, and read credentials by name from the environment. If a capability exists only as a vendor plugin, raise a consult to kai; the exception is a CTO line with an exit plan.

rules.title: Operating model: the lead plans and adjudicates, workers execute and return receipts
rules.body: Operating model (CTO standing order 2026-09-17, docs/SOP_PLAN_AND_EXECUTE.md, THE_WAY s16): 1. The lead plans, adjudicates, integrates accepted source, issues gates and records; the lead does not execute delivery steps. 2. Workers execute in their roster lane end to end and return receipts; they never merge to canonical or issue gates. 3. Every dispatch names the goal, the gate it feeds, and the exact acceptance receipt per step. 4. Every return is a completion_handback with the reviewed tip SHA and the receipts, or a consult with options; never silence, never a self-granted workaround. 5. One handoff per worker per lane at a time; parallelism is across workers. 6. Irreversible steps (deletion, reset, restore-over, public publish, spend) need a CTO line.

rules.title: Permanent main workspace and document custody (CTO 2026-09-08)
rules.body:
# Permanent workspace and document home

CTO instruction, 2026-09-08:

> Always work, store files and maintain `/Users/amadmalik/DevVault/helix` as the main root folder. Treat `/Users/amadmalik/DevVault/kaidera-os-worktrees` as temporary.

Use `/Users/amadmalik/DevVault/helix` as the default working directory and permanent home for project documents, plans, research, evidence and deliverables. Keep each lane's documents in its existing folder within this root; KOS release documents live in `Program/KOS/`.

Temporary worktrees may isolate a bounded source change or verification run when necessary. They are not a permanent document home or an alternative project root. Before handoff or completion, consolidate documents and required evidence into the main root, reconcile existing edits, and verify the copies. Link users and future agents to the main-root paths. Historical execution paths and source hashes in immutable receipts remain unchanged as provenance.

Preserve active edits and unique evidence when consolidating. Do not delete temporary worktrees until their work is safely retained and their owners are finished. Consolidating documents does not merge, deploy or qualify product code; the existing source-review and release gates still apply.

Generated `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` remain generated from Cortex. Record this instruction in Cortex and the project documentation, not by hand-editing generated pointers.

rules.title: The SDLC loop every lead runs (CTO 2026-09-03)
rules.body:
Every epic, feature, fix, incident, review and plan runs the Kaidera AI-native SDLC loop (skill `kaidera-sdlc`, design 31, CTO standing order 2026-09-03): INTENT -> GRILL -> SPEC -> PLAN -> BUILD <-> VERIFY -> REVIEW -> SHIP -> MAINTAIN, with incidents and findings re-entering as intent.

The part that always holds:
1. Nothing is implemented without an accepted plan (files that change, order, risks, proof); departing from the plan updates the plan in the same commit.
2. Grill before you build: one question at a time; facts are looked up, decisions are put to the human; stop at shared understanding.
3. Verification is output that can fail, pasted from the final tree; a green suite is not evidence of behaviour; a bug fix starts with a failing test that is never edited to pass.
4. Review separates duties: the author never approves; Ren's adversarial review, kai's adjudication, then merge.
5. The agent acts up to the gate and cannot pass it: merge to main, deploy, publish and release wait for the named human authorisation (the CTO's go).
6. Mistake twice, rule once; incidents become intent and evals; every rule is a dated decision with evidence and a reopening trigger.

The skill carries the depth (references, templates, evals). Load it at the start of any work and cite the stage you are in.
